parties.counterparty: Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL)

plans.note: Primary cap/consequential-damages waiver sits in 15.3 within Section 15.0; check mutuality, dollar cap and carve-outs (IP indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence). Also review the Equipment/Program Loan Agreement Section 15 (Limitation of Remedies) and Section 13 disclaimer, plus the CI Agreement Section 7 disclaimers, which are IBM-drafted and may already favour us — do not flag those.

MSL indemnity is expressly scoped in 15.1 with payment/cooperation mechanics in 15.2; confirm third-party IP infringement and personal injury/property damage coverage and that any IBM-side indemnity stays narrow. Attachment 6 warranties/Microsoft appendix obligations may add related protections.

No non-compete on IBM is apparent; the only restriction-flavoured provisions are 14.18 (Restrictions and Limitations, integration services) and 16.15 (Prohibited Suppliers, which restricts MSL's sourcing, not our business). Confirm 14.18 does not limit IBM's ability to build or buy elsewhere before concluding absent.

Check Scope of Work (3.0) and Purchase of Products (6.0 of the SOW/Product Attachment) for any commitment that IBM source Products solely from MSL; forecast (11.0) and IBM Parts provisions (8.1) may create de facto sole-source language. If only volume forecasts exist, treat under MINCOMMIT rather than double-flagging.

Pricing sections (7.0/7.1/7.2, 14.14 Integration price, 8.2 Parts Cost Reductions, Appendix 1 Mark Up) are where any best-price/most-favoured pricing language would sit. MFN running in IBM's favour is welcome and must not be flagged; only an obligation on IBM to give MSL best terms is a deviation.

Personnel (9.0) covers transferred employees and is the likeliest home for any hiring restriction on IBM; also scan 16.7 (Assignees and Visits) and 5.2 (Relationship Management) for named-personnel constraints. Accept narrow, time-limited restrictions with a general-advertising carve-out.

Termination architecture is Section 5.0 (5.1 Breach, 5.2 Rights Upon Termination, 5.3 Prices Upon Termination) read with Term (4.0 base / 2.0 SOW). Test whether IBM has a convenience right on reasonable notice, whether MSL has a symmetric right (unacceptable mid-term), and whether 5.3 imposes penalty pricing or wind-down charges on exit.

Term clauses (base 4.0, SOW 2.0, Loan Agreement Section 2) are the only places an evergreen/auto-renewal and notice window could appear; if the term is fixed with extension only by mutual written agreement, the rule is satisfied and no auto-renewal exit mechanic is needed.

16.9 Governing Law is the operative clause; confirm the chosen state (New York/Delaware/California acceptable) and that disputes go to courts rather than offshore arbitration. Cross-check the CI Agreement Section 8 and Loan Agreement Section 16 general clauses for a conflicting law/venue choice.

16.2 Assignment plus 16.5 Sale or Merger are the key provisions: verify IBM may assign to affiliates/successors without consent and that MSL cannot terminate or re-price on an IBM change of control, while MSL assignment remains consent-gated.

Section 13.0 (Intellectual and Industrial Property) with 13.3 Licenses governs ownership; also check tooling ownership (20.0, 21.0/21.1), title provisions (19.4) and the Loan Agreement Section 5 (Ownership and License). Confirm no assignment of IBM IP, data or IBM Classified Parts information to MSL.

Licence scope lives in 13.3 (Licenses) and, for loaned programs, Loan Agreement Sections 5/6 and 12.2; Attachment 6 and Appendix A (Microsoft authorization) contain further grant terms. Note that most grants here run from IBM to MSL — only grants to IBM that are revocable at will or exclude our affiliates/contractors are deviations.

Section 7.0 Audit, 16.14 Records, Attachment 6 Section 4.0 and Appendix A Section 4 all appear to give IBM audit rights against MSL, which benefits us and must not be flagged. Flag only any reciprocal right for MSL to audit IBM's usage/records that lacks notice, frequency and cost limits.

Delinquency-based profit-rate tables (7.2 / Shipment Profit Rate schedules) and 10.4 Delays in Shipment operate as credits against MSL and are in our favour. The exposure to review is Premium Cost (9.0), PO cancellation charges (6.1), supply flexibility and EOL inventory liability (13.2/13.3) imposing penalty-like payments on IBM.

MSL warranties appear in 14.2 (base) and SOW 19.0 (scope, exclusions, turnaround, epidemic failure) plus Attachment 6 Section 3.0. Assess duration, remedy (repair/replace/credit), the 19.6 implied-warranty disclaimer and whether 16.19 expiration of representations cuts the period too short.

No insurance heading appears anywhere; the closest analogues are risk-of-loss/care provisions (Loan Agreement Section 8, 21.2 Care of tooling, 13.1 Consigned Products) and the premises lease (10.0). Confirm no embedded insurance covenant before recording as missing, since MSL occupies IBM premises and holds consigned inventory.

Look for take-or-pay style exposure in Purchase of Products/PO cancellation (6.0, 6.1), Product Forecast and requirements-accuracy commitments (11.0, 11.3, Appendix 2), and inventory/EOL liability (13.2, 13.3, 13.4, Appendix 4). Flag only if IBM must pay for unordered volumes or excess inventory without an exit; otherwise note the fallback.

Section 12.0 Transition Services and 5.2 Rights Upon Termination are the primary hooks, supported by 13.4 Sale of Inventory, Attachment 6 Section 3 (Obligations Upon Termination) and Loan Agreement Section 12/12.1 (return of loaned items). Verify duration of assistance, pricing at then-current rates, and return/destruction of IBM confidential information, tooling and data.
